newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK regulators say watching unsual stock movements.
newsitem.headline: HK regulators say watching unsual stock movements.

text.p: Hong Kong securities regulators and the stock exchange said they were concerned about recent unusual price and volume movements in some shares, and warned they would take all necessary action to prevent abuses.

The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said in a joint statement they would continue to conduct detailed enquiries into companies, brokers and investors involved in unusual share trading.
They would also require a greater level of disclosure by companies in relation to rumours, prospects of transactions, approaches by third parties and the use of placing proceeds.

"Where warranted, the SFC and the Exchange are prepared to use their powers to refuse approval of transactions, listing of new shares or derivatives where the company has been the subject of unexplained unusual trading activities or ... has previously denied any knowledge of possible approaches/transactions which subsequently eventuate," they said.

The two said they would suspend trade in shares subject to persistent unusual trading and institute investigations, and warned such suspensions may be prolonged until they were satisfied fair and orderly trading could take place.
